label: Updated 12 PM ET
title: Today In Golf
summary: A 30-second briefing on today’s biggest golf stories.

items.headline: Rolapp Faces Scheduling Warning
items.text: Stephen Gallacher warned Brian Rolapp that forcing PGA Tour stars into a signature-event-heavy schedule is unlikely to work, since top players like Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler prefer playing about 20 events a year rather than a condensed 30-event mandate.

items.headline: DeChambeau Pushes LIV Survival
items.text: Bryson DeChambeau expressed surprise at Saudi Arabia’s PIF ending LIV Golf funding after 2026 but remains optimistic, working to secure $250–$350 million in new investment and shift LIV to a 10-event team-golf model while trying to regain form after missing cuts at the Masters and PGA.

items.headline: Clark, Koepka Withdraw from Charles Schwab
items.text: Wyndham Clark and Brooks Koepka both withdrew from the Charles Schwab Challenge before it started, removing two recent major champions and significant star power from the Colonial field.
